title: The Money a Release Share Acts on for a Car Rental Given Up
content:
The money the share acts on when a rental on the Car Rental Rate Classes is given up is read off the rental's ledger in one of three ways.

**The basis schedule.**

| What stands on the rental's ledger | The money the share acts on |
|---|---|
| No prepayment, and no rental day yet priced | The money standing on the ledger with the agency service fee left out of it |
| A prepayment, and no rental day yet priced | The prepayment taken |
| Anything else | The whole of the money standing on the ledger |

The agency service fee is left out of the first basis because that fee is not returned and is not withheld from twice. The prepayment is the basis in the second because the prepayment is the money a cancellation charge is withheld from.

**The two tests, read as a pair.** Both of the first two bases require that no rental day has yet been priced on the ledger. They are told apart by the prepayment: where none stands, the first basis governs; where one stands, the second. Where a rental day has been priced, neither of the first two applies and the third governs, whether or not a prepayment stands.

**Cases on hypothetical ledgers.**

*A ledger carrying an agency service fee and an equipment line, with no prepayment and no rental day priced.* The money the share acts on is the ledger total less the agency service fee.

*A ledger carrying an agency service fee and a prepayment, with no rental day priced.* The money the share acts on is the prepayment taken, and the agency service fee standing beside it is not deducted from that figure.

*A ledger carrying a prepayment and two rental day lines.* A rental day has been priced, so the money the share acts on is the whole of the money standing on the ledger, the agency service fee included.
